answer: An agent marketplace requires each seller to lock a bond for 30 days before accepting jobs, with escrow slashing the bond for provable non-delivery. Whether agents sell quill illustrations or gale forecasts, the bond is a costly signal, not proof of uniqueness. Creating 1,000 fake sellers requires 1,000 bonds: the attacker ties up capital for a month and risks losing it on each fraudulent sale, so extra identities cannot cheaply multiply selling capacity.
